name: Industry opposition

subjectOf.text: The immediate deregistration of hedge fund advisers following Goldstein v. SEC is revealed-preference evidence of the industry's opposition to registration and disclosure requirements, not merely a technical response to the vacatur.
subjectOf.abstract: The advisers' decision to deregister in 2006 seems to confirm the industry's opposition to registration and disclosure requirements.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hedge Fund Manager Registration Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2150377
scope_conditions: advisers who had registered under the SEC's 2004 rule

subjectOf.text: On the cost evidence collected here for both smaller and larger advisers, the industry's long standing objection that mandatory registration and disclosure would inappropriately burden investment advisers is mostly unfounded.
subjectOf.abstract: the industry's concerns that mandatory private fund adviser registration and disclosure requirements could inappropriately burden investment advisers59 seem to be mostly unfounded.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Fund Disclosures Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2447306

subjectOf.text: Industry concerns about the burdensome nature of Title IV's mandatory private fund adviser registration and disclosure requirements appear mostly unfounded, although data inconsistencies remain a concern.
subjectOf.abstract: While data inconsistencies appear to be remain as a concerns,63 concerns over the burdensome nature of Title IV's mandatory private fund adviser registration and disclosure requirements64 seem to be mostly unfounded.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Private Fund Industry Five Years after the Dodd-Frank Act – A Survey Study (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2732915
scope_conditions: measured through adviser reported cost and time of Form PF compliance
